nodes.description: Abnormal brain MRI in about half of individuals, with dysplastic or abnormal corpus callosum, cortical atrophy, focal cortical dysplasia and hypoplastic olfactory bulbs.

evidence.snippet: The features in those with abnormalities are variable and include: dysplastic or abnormal corpus callosum, cortical atrophy, focal cortical dysplasia, and hypoplastic olfactory bulbs.

nodes.description: Dosage reduction of critical-region genes disturbs craniofacial morphogenesis, giving the recognizable facial gestalt.

evidence.snippet: Distinct facial features, including long face with high anterior hairline, epicanthal folds, hypertelorism, downslanting palpebral fissures, sparse and broad medial eyebrows, broad and/or depressed nasal bridge, long smooth philtrum, and small mouth with full lower lip were common in all individuals.

nodes.description: Prenatal and postnatal growth retardation with short stature and feeding difficulties is common, while a subset develop childhood obesity, so growth parameters are variable.

evidence.snippet: However, in later childhood, growth parameters were extremely variable with nearly 30% of individuals still exhibiting postnatal growth retardation and short stature, while 17% had obesity.

nodes.description: Genital anomalies affect a majority of affected males and include hypospadias, micropenis and cryptorchidism.

evidence.snippet: Genital abnormalities are reported in a majority of individuals (60%) and include hypospadias, microphallus, and cryptorchidism.

nodes.description: Reduced dosage of critical-region genes disturbs brain development, producing developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia and, in a subset, autism spectrum disorder.

evidence.snippet: It is characterized by growth retardation, intellectual disability, and distinct facial features

evidence.reference_title: A large-scale survey of the novel 15q24 microdeletion syndrome in autism spectrum disorders identifies an atypical deletion that narrows the critical region.
evidence.snippet: The 15q24 microdeletion syndrome has been recently described as a recurrent, submicroscopic genomic imbalance found in individuals with intellectual disability, typical facial appearance, hypotonia, and digital and genital abnormalities.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular and phenotypic characteristics of 15q24 microdeletion in pediatric patients with developmental disorders.
evidence.snippet: Chromosome 15q24 microdeletion is a rare genetic disorder characterized by development delay, facial dysmorphism, congenital malformations, and occasional autism spectrum disorder (ASD).

nodes.description: Behavior abnormalities (autism, hyperactivity, aggression, attention deficit disorder) in about 37% of individuals.

evidence.snippet: Behavior abnormalities, such as autism, hyperactivity, aggression, and attention deficit disorder have been reported in 37% individuals with 15q24 deletion syndrome.

nodes.description: Behavioral therapy for the autism, hyperactivity and attention problems seen in a substantial minority of individuals.

evidence.snippet: Behavioral therapy may benefit individuals with this syndrome.

nodes.description: Non-allelic homologous recombination between the paralogous low-copy repeat clusters flanking 15q24 generates a recurrent interstitial deletion of 1.7-6.1 Mb, removing one copy of every gene in the interval.

evidence.snippet: The deletions range in size from 1.7-6.1 Mb and usually result from nonallelic homologous recombination (NAHR) between paralogous low-copy repeats (LCRs).
In addition, many individuals were reported to have joint laxity and scoliosis.
